sentences.text:
Charge u/s. 420 IPC & u/s. 4/5/6 of Prize Chits & Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act 1978,
was ordered to be framed against revisionist/accused Sulekh Aggarwal in case FIR No. 27/2009 PS EOW, vide order on charge dated 16.09.2022 where all except the revisionist were discharged,
which paved the way for the instant revision as the revisionist is aggrieved by the same.

sentences.text: The revision so emerging is hereby disposed off through this order.

2. Before adverting into the details of the contentions raised by the contesting sides, the background in the shape of the indispensable facts, against the backdrop of which, the FIR and thereafter the charge-sheet and the order on charge emerged are required to be looked into.
3. The genesis of the case lies in the scheme allegedly floated by KBC Mart Pvt. Ltd., which was being headed by the revisionist herein as its Managing Director.
The aforesaid company wsa registered with the object of providing all kinds of agriculture, industrial, consumer daily use items for business houses, depot, branches and shops, etc. to the consumers.

4. According to the revisionist himself in terms of para 2, point 2 of the Revision, the incidental and ancillary objects were also available to the company to advance, deposit with money lending securities as well as to sell articles for business development and to share profits in any union of interest, joint venture, reciprocal concession or companies involved in similar business or transaction.

The scheme floated by the company consisted of two items i.e. a pant and shirt piece and sale of suit length and the persons, who purchase these cloths against a consideration of Rs.1500/- and Rs.3500/- respectively, were given an option to involve other persons and to avail the benefit of the scheme in which a sum of Rs.100/- was to be paid to the person, who brings a new person on every such additional member.

It is asserted by the revisionist that there is no complaint Sulekh Aggarwal vs State on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14456944/
1 that the person who deposited the aforesaid amount of Rs.1500/- and Rs.3500/- did not get either the pant shirt piece or suit piece.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The scheme in itself does not violate any law and for that matter similar other schemes are in vogue, for instance, if you purchase medicine from Apollo Pharmacy,
they offer you 10% discount on the MRP and for that matter if you use credit card and the spending through the credit card brings him certain points which can be utilized to purchase the items on offer with the credit card from various companies and entities.
In these circumstances, the revisionist did not do anything wrong and so far as the charge framed u/s. 420 IPC & u/s. 4/5/6 of Prize Chits & Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act 1978.

entities.text: Prize Chits & Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act 1978
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The same cannot be there as the acts of the revisionist is not covered under the provisions of the said Acts.

5. With the aforesaid contentions, it is also submitted that the revisionist also deserves to be discharged as other persons namely Sweety Aggarwal, Mukesh Jain and Narender Kumar, all Directors of KBC Mart Pvt. Ltd. were discharged.
Simply because the revisionist happens to be the Managing Director does not mean that he can be held responsible for the offences alleged when no such offence in fact took place.

There is not a single person who has lodged a complaint that he was not given the benefit of the pant shirt and suit length scheme or that the revisionist has deceived or taken anyone for a ride and cheated him.
6. Ld.

Substitute Prosecutor contended that the contentions raised on behalf of the revisionist are beyond and contrary to the facts on record inasmuch as the statements of the persons, who have been deceived, are there u/s.161 Cr.P.C. together with certain hand written complaints against the revisionist.
There is not one person but score of persons were cheated and the list goes around 800 persons or so.
There are cogent evidence against the revisionist as not only the brochure of the schemes, photographs etc, were there whereby he is seen to be promoting the schemes but complicit in everything.

It is unusual that somebody, who wants to have cloths, would instead of buying the cloths from a cloth store, would go to the company of the revisionist for these things, unless something else is promised and that "something else" is the reason why people approached the revisionist comapny.

That 'something' comes out in the statement of the victims recorded u/s.161 Cr.P.C.
7.

The record also contains invitation card of some sort of pre-launching ceremony which seems to be a kind of open invitation for all inasmuch as relatives and friends were also invited there as can be seen printed on the card.

What kind of pre-launching ceremony was there, is not clear from the invitation card but the application form, which has also been seized gives some idea that merely selling the cloths was not the idea.
Why would a cloth merchant require applicant's vital information in the application form i.e. date of birth, anniversary, email ID, nominee, so on and so forth.

This form itself reflects that it is some sort of privileged customership but no further details are available in the application form apart from the terms and conditions printed on the back of the Form.

The brochure of the revisionist company reflects some sort of activities which are beyond the sale of cloths and some deposits seems to be coming where TDS too was to be deducted and on different stages, different amounts become payable or in lieu of the payment, it seems some articles were offered.
The printed words reflect sponsoring income.
Such kind of schemes cannot be treated as simple sale of cloths, as has been tried to be portrayed.
Various other incentives have been offered which ranges from DVD Players to a bungalow worth Rs.50 lakhs plus Rs.1 crore cash, etc.

sentences.text: 2 Evidently, this is not simple and plain sale of cloths and incentives on new membership secured by erstwhile members.

8. At this stage, when the statements of the victims are to be looked into including the hand-written complaints of various persons then it appears that it was sort of investment that the revisionist was collecting money from various persons in various investment schemes promising them exhorbitant returns that too within a very short span of time.
That is how people got cheated since the revisionist thereafter closed his shop/office and vanished.
Not only that, the complaint reflects that those who persisted with their complaints with him, were threatened as well.
Score of such complaints are there from various persons and according to the prosecution, the number at least goes upto 800 such pesons.
Therefore, in these circumstances, it is submitted that the challenge to the impugned order is improper and should not be allowed.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the contesting sides and have perused the record as well.

10. It is settled proposition of law that at the time of framing of charge, the Court is not required to marshal any evidence and only grave suspicion is to be seen and when grave suspicion arises, charge can be framed against the accused.

Reliance can be placed upon Alpana Dass v. CBI 2006 (90) DRJ 441.
11.
In the case of Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal 1979 SSC (3) 609, their lordship laid down the parameters that must weigh in the mind of the Court while considering the issue on charge.

entities.text: Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal 1979 SSC (3) 609
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ( iii )
The test to determine a prima facie case would naturally depend upon the facts of each case and it is difficult to lay down a rule of universal application.

By and large however if two views are equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence produced before him while giving rise to some suspicion but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused.

(iv) That in exercising his jurisdiction u/s.227 of the Code the Judge which under the present Code is a senior and experienced Court cannot act merely as a Post Office or a mouthpiece of the prosecution, but has to consider the broad probabilities of the Sulekh Aggarwal vs State on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14456944/
3 case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court,
any basic infirmities appearing in the case and so on.

entities.text: Sulekh Aggarwal vs State on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This however, does not mean that the Judge should make a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial.

12. Under Section 397 Cr.PC, the revisional Court is required to see the correctness, legality or proprietary of any finding, sentence or order and also to see that there is no irregularity in the proceedings.

While interpreting the scope and ambit of Section 397 Cr.PC, it has been observed in the Judgment of "Amarnath vs. State of Haryana, 1977 SC 2185" that the powers of revision conferred by Sub- section (1) shall not be exercised in relation to any interlocutory order passed in any appeal, inquiry, trial or other proceeding".

entities.text: Amarnath vs. State of Haryana, 1977 SC 2185
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So it should not be an interlocutory order qua which a revision can be filed.
13. It is thus evident that the scope of revision is confined and limited to the aforesaid parameters and the contentions of the revisionist are required to be appreciated accordingly.

As such, the impugned order is to be examined in the parameters and scope of the revision and to ascertain as to whether there is any illegality, irregularity or any procedural lapse which may require intervention by the revisional court.
14. At the stage of the charge, only a first hand opinion is to be formed as to whether an offence has been committed by a person or not.
If it is shown prima facie that such and such offence is committed by a person then that is enough to frame the charge and to proceed with the trial.

In the instant case, there are numerous complaints against the revisionist and all those complaints are more or less on the same lines that persons were assured a kind of disproportionate return on their deposits and to lure them, the revisionist under the aegis of his KBC Mart Pvt. Ltd. conducted various launching ceremonies and programmes and offered them suit length and pant shirt pieces with an in-built mechanism schemes to bring more persons and have incentives.

Ultimately, it reflects that some kind of investment in installments were to be made, as can be seen from the receipts of money deposits with the company of the revisionist and the schedule of payments given in brochure/literature of the company.
The promised return was not to come and has not been made and not only that the revisionist closed his shop/office, which trepidated the investors/customers of the revisionist.
People were not getting promised return and for that matter, their own money was stuck up.
The revisionist allegedly threatened his subscribers/customers that is why the present FIR came into being with the EoW of Delhi Police.
15. The arguments addressed on behalf of the revisionist are bald that there is no complainant, no one was deceived as nobody can claim that promised clothes were not delivered to him or her.

However, there is no explanation as to where from the revisionist was to generate the money to give incentives to the persons who brought in fresh subscribers/investors to avail the schemes offered by the revisionist.

The record further reflects that money was being deposited by KBC Mart Pvt. Ltd.
under the care and control of the revisionist herein.

According to the clarification received by the Investigating Officer from the RBI through the letter dated 02.06.2009, the company run by the revisionist was not registered with RBI as Non-Banking Financial Company, therefore, was not Sulekh Aggarwal vs State on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14456944/
4 authorised to accept public deposits.
This brings in the provisions of Prize Chits & Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act 1978 into play.

sentences.text:
All these goes on to show that the opinion formed by the Ld. Trial Court is supported by record and there is nothing which may be termed as illegal,
inappropriate or perverse rendering the impugned order vulnerable to be challenged and assailed in the revision.
16.
In view of these facts and circumstances, there is no flaw in the impugned order which requires intervention.
As a result, the revision stands dismissed.

17. Nothing expressed herein shall tantamount to any expression on the merits of the case and the Ld. Judge will proceed with the matter as per law without being guided by any observations made in this order.
18. Trial court record be sent back with copy of this order.
Revision file be consigned to the Record Room.
